title: VenusMine identifies PET hydrolase KbPETase
summary: VenusMine combines structure-based search with protein-language-model representations and learned property filters to prioritize candidate PET hydrolases from large sequence collections. The authors tested 34 selected proteins and report PET-hydrolyzing activity for 14; KbPETase had an optimum activity temperature 32 °C above the IsPETase comparator. This is laboratory enzyme evidence, not demonstrated waste-processing performance. A 2024 preprint reportedly contains an earlier version; its exact version-to-result chronology was not freshly resolved, so this draft uses the journal version date and does not claim first discovery priority.
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

evidence.tested: 34 selected proteins were tested; the source reports PET-hydrolyzing activity for 14 and characterizes KbPETase experimentally.
evidence.unknown: Scale-up, real-world plastic-waste processing, independent replication and exact relation of the earlier preprint’s experiments remain outside this bounded review.
evidence.ai_role: VenusMine uses structure search, protein-language-model embeddings and learned property predictions to select enzyme candidates for experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary article text including title, methods, results and publication metadata; direct PMC open triggered CAPTCHA.
